newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Govt must not cut Australia bank competition - Labor.
newsitem.headline: Govt must not cut Australia bank competition - Labor.

text.p: Any banking policy reforms made by the Liberal/National government in the wake of the Wallis Financial System Inquiry should not cut competition, Labor Opposition Leader Kim Beazley said on Monday.
Beazley also said he was concerned Westpac Banking Corp's proposed A$1.435 billion takeover of Bank of Melbourne Ltd would reduce competition.
"We don't want to get into a situation where there's less competition...we're going to be looking at the Wallis Inquiry from that point of view," Beazley told reporters in Launceston.
He said the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) should examine whether the Westpac/Bank of Melbourne takeover would cut competition.
The ACCC is currently examining the takeover and is expected to decide whether or not to approve it within a month to six weeks.

The Wallis Inquiry's report is due to be released later this week and is widely expected to recommend the government ease rules currently stopping Australia's major banks from merging with each other.
